business_problem: BMW Group needed to scale industrial AI across quality assurance, production, and logistics, but limited training data, manual image labeling, and a lack of end-to-end lifecycle tooling slowed model development and made it hard for plant teams to deploy AI autonomously.
solution_summary: BMW Group built a complete deep learning operations pipeline on NVIDIA DGX systems so manufacturing teams could generate training data, train models, and deploy AI applications from one platform. Using NVIDIA Omniverse Enterprise, the company creates virtual factories and synthetic production scenes that feed the SORDI dataset, the open industrial reference set BMW uses for object detection, segmentation, and related vision tasks. DGX systems with Hopper architecture then train synthetic-data generators and downstream quality models, while TAO inside NVIDIA AI Enterprise supports AutoML and inference for no-code applications such as LabelTool Lite. This lets employees load a few examples, enrich them with synthetic images, and quickly build visual-inspection models for tasks like door-sill validation and stitch checking. The result is an industrial AI stack that reduces manual labeling, speeds deployment, and makes advanced quality-automation tooling usable well beyond the R&D team.

data_flow: Synthetic factory scenes are generated in Omniverse, converted into large labeled datasets such as SORDI, trained on DGX systems, and then pushed into no-code and production QA workflows where plant employees deploy inspection models with minimal manual labeling.
business_outcome: BMW achieved an 8x boost in data-science productivity, 4–6x better performance than legacy systems, cut employee time to implement QA automation by more than two-thirds, and can generate hundreds of thousands of synthetic images on demand to support production AI at scale.
